steps.message:
# Merge duplicate billing tickets

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service, which you can use through the `tickets` MCP server.

Some open tickets of the billing team are duplicates. Two open billing tickets are duplicates when they have the same customer and name the same order: the order number is on the line that starts with `Order:` in the ticket body.

For every group of duplicates:

1. Keep the ticket with the lowest id open and unchanged.
2. Set every other ticket of the group to status `duplicate`.
3. Add exactly one comment to each ticket you set to `duplicate`, with the text `Duplicate of #<id>`, where `<id>` is the id of the ticket that stays open.

Only open tickets of the billing team count. Do not change, comment on or create any other ticket.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by discovering the tickets MCP tools.

I merged the duplicate billing tickets and wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`. There were 29 open billing tickets and 6 duplicate groups, matched on the same customer and the same `Order:` number.

| Kept open (lowest id) | Set to `duplicate` |
|---|---|
| #101 | #118, #122 |
| #103 | #123 |
| #105 | #112, #120 |
| #108 | #111 |
| #117 | #124 |
| #127 | #128 |

Each of the 8 duplicates got one `Duplicate of #<id>` comment pointing to the ticket that stays open. I didn't touch any other ticket.

Several calls failed along the way (429, 503, 504, and a truncated response for ticket 111), and I retried each one. The comment on #118 timed out, so I retried it with the same idempotency key. A search for billing tickets with status `duplicate` returned a total of 8, and #118 has exactly one comment.

Some groups, like #105, #112 and #120, have different titles but the same customer and order. I treated them as duplicates because your definition only uses customer and order.
